Therefore, any product that is used directly after production is called the final product.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Which income wise classification category can country ‘Q’ be put in based on its level of development? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"Based on the level of development, ‘Q’ can be classified as an upper middle class income developing country. The World Bank has divided the countries of the world into three main divisions on the basis of per capita gross national income. These are High Income, Middle Income and Low Income countries. The Middle Income countries have been further segmented into Upper Middle and Lower Middle income countries. The countries where the per capita income of the people is between 4466 USD to 13845 USD, those countries are called upper middle income countries. Again, the countries of the world have been divided into three groups based on their level of development, namely, underdeveloped, developing and developed countries. Mainly, upper middle income countries are called developing countries. In the stem we can see that the per capita income of country ‘Q’ is 7900 USD. The country can be classified as an upper middle income country based on the level of income. Again, based on the level of development, the upper middle income countries are called developing countries. So it can be said that based on the level of development, ‘Q’ can be classified as a upper middle class income developing country.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Which medium between ‘M’ and ‘N’ play a more important role in converting country ‘R’ based on per capita income to country ‘Q’ based on per capita income? Give your opinion.","marks":4,"answer":"Between ‘N’ and ‘M’, ‘N’ that is planned development programs play a more important role in converting country ‘R’ to country ‘Q’. According to the classification of countries by World Bank, which is based on per capita gross national income, countries that have a per capita income of more than 13845 USD are called high income countries. And these high-income countries are developed countries. The countries where the per capita income of people are between 1136 USD to 4465 USD, are called lower middle income countries. Although the lower middle income countries are called developing countries, but basically they fall in the category of underdeveloped countries. To convert an underdeveloped country like ‘R’ (with per capita income 1460 USD) into a developing upper middle income country like ‘Q’ (7900 USD), planned development programs (‘N’) are more crucial than merely having an advanced agricultural system (‘M’). Planned development ensures systematic investment in infrastructure, education, healthcare, industrialization, and good governance, which are essential for sustained economic growth and structural transformation.\n---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

These policies include ‘National Agriculture Extension Policy,’ ‘National Seed Policy,’ ‘Integrated Fertilizer Distribution Policy’ and ‘Integrated Pest Management.’ Moreover, activities for agricultural development are going on according to the ‘National Agriculture Policy 1999.’ Under these policies, the government is expanding area of agricultural land through eradicating water logging from different regions of the country and through planned water extraction from marshy land. The government is also investing heavily in disbursing agricultural and rural loans through banks and financial institutions and in producing and supplying high quality seeds. As a result of all these steps, the former food grain dependent Bangladesh has been able to achieve self-sufficiency in food grain production today. parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"Define GNP.","marks":1,"answer":"The monetary value of the amount of material and immaterial goods and services produced in a particular period generally in one year by investing the labour and capital of a country in the natural resources or land of that country is called Gross National Product or GNP.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Explain the process of determining standard of living through per capita income.","marks":2,"answer":"Per capita income determines the standard of living of an individual. Along with high per capita income, the issue of the price of goods has also to be taken into consideration to determine the standard of life. If the per capita income of the people of a country in a year becomes double and at the same time the level of prices of goods also becomes double, the real standard of living will remain the same. Because financial income and the prices of goods have increased at the same rate. However, if per capita income increases while the price level remains unchanged, the standard of living will increase, and if per capita income decreases, the standard of living will decline.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the socio-economic infrastructure of the 'A' category countries of the above table.","marks":3,"answer":"Norway and Sweden can be defined as high-income countries or developed countries. The type of country where economic development has taken place and development has been continuing for a long term is called a developed country. The socioeconomic infrastructure of these countries is developed, the industrial sector is expanded, the transport and communication systems are developed and international trade is in favour of the economy. Housing, education facilities, and health services for the people of those countries are ensured. Because of the expansion of education, knowledge, and science are also expanded rapidly and new technologies are invented. These countries have achieved this developed state because of reaching the top stage of the development process. The per capita income of these countries is such that after meeting all basic needs of the people huge amount of money remains as surplus- which is spent in forming savings and capital. So, the socio-economic infrastructures of these countries are much developed.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"'C' category countries can be turned into 'B' and 'B' into 'A' by maintaining relationship with each other-Give your opinion.","marks":4,"answer":"‘C’ category countries, the underdeveloped countries can be turned into ‘B’, as well as developing countries can be turned into ‘A’ category or developed countries. An underdeveloped country requires suitable policies to be implemented to ensure the overall socioeconomic development of the country. Agricultural resources should be utilized to form the import, and export sectors. In the same way, developing countries can be turned into developed countries by empowering industry, increasing foreign trade, etc. The policy-based foundation of the economy should be followed. People in developing countries can be turned into human resources to utilize the natural resources of that country. Thus, underdeveloped countries can be turned into developing countries likewise, developing countries can be turned into developed countries by following the above-mentioned steps.\n---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is GDP?","marks":1,"answer":"Gross domestic product is the sum total of the value of the final level of goods and services produced by all the people living within the geographical boundaries of a country at a given time.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"What does the vicious cycle of poverty means? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"An important concept in economics is the vicious cycle of poverty. Its main proponent is the economist Ragnar Narks. If the per capita income of the people is low, all the income has to be spent on the consumption of daily necessities. Due to this, the savings rate of the people decreases. As a result, there is a shortage of capital. Investment decreases and jobs are not created, so unemployment increases. Per capita income is decreasing. In this way, it is called the vicious cycle of poverty.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Which category does ‘X’ country belong to on the basis of per capita income? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"The ‘X’ country referred to in the stimulus on the basis of per capita income is a middle-income country. The World Bank divides the countries of the world into three main categories based on gross national income per capita. These are high-income countries, middle-income countries and low-income countries. Middle-income countries have been divided into two categories – upper middle income countries and lower middle income countries. Countries whose per capita income ranges from $1136 to $4465 are called lower middle income countries. Again, on the basis of the level of development, the countries of the world are divided into three categories: developed, developing and underdeveloped. Basically, lower middle income countries are called developing countries. The stimulus shows that X has a national income of $6400 crore and per capita income = 6400/2 = $3,200 per capita. On the basis of income level, the country is included in the lower middle income country. Again, on the basis of the level of development, the lower middle income countries are called developing countries. So it can be said that on the basis of per capita income, the X country is a lower middle income country.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Do you think that the standard of living of people of ‘Y’ country is better than that of ‘X’ country? Give reasons for your answer.","marks":4,"answer":"Yes, the standard of living of the people of Y country i.e. upper middle income country is better than X country i.e. lower middle income country. Middle-income countries are divided into two groups: upper middle income countries and lower middle income countries. The basic needs of the people of these countries have been fulfilled to a great extent. Countries are rapidly industrializing and social infrastructure, such as education and healthcare, is rapidly developing upwards. In the above table, we can see that the national income of the X country is $ 6400 crore and the per capita income is US $ 3200. It is a lower-middle-income country based on per capita income. Again Y country's gross national income is $ 7500 crore and per capita income is US $ 5000 (7500/1.5). It is included in the upper middle income country. Since the per capita income of country X is low and has achieved some improvement through planned economic development, the standard of living will be slightly lower than that of Y country. Because the per capita income of Y country is 5000 US dollars. Although where the price of the commodity is 200 dollars per kg, the living standard of the people will be better than that of X country due to higher per capita income. Because the population of country Y is less than that of country X. In conclusion, the standard of living of the people of country Y is more advanced than the X country.\n---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is utility?","marks":1,"answer":"Utility is the ability of a product to meet human needs.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Explain the role of entrepreneurs in production.","marks":2,"answer":"The risk or uncertainty in production is borne by the organizer or entrepreneur. Entrepreneurs integrate the three factors of production, namely – land, labour and capital. All types of risks or uncertainties related to production is also borne by the entrepreneur. This is why, an entrepreneur is another important factor of production system.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Determine, with explanation, the gross national product (GNP) of the country described in the stem.","marks":3,"answer":"The gross national product (GNP) of the country described in the stem is determined below. Gross National Product is the total financial value of the final goods and services produced, within a specific time period (usually 1 year), by the citizens of this country living within the country and outside the geographical boundaries. In order to determine gross national product, income of citizens living and employed abroad is added and income of foreigners living in the country is deducted. In this case, if we denote income of citizens living abroad with ‘X’ and income of foreigners living in the country with ‘M,’ then GNP = Gross Domestic Product (GDP) + (X-M). ∴ Gross National Product of the country is GNP = GDP + (X-M) = (28,000 + (7000 - 3000)) crore taka = (28,000 + 4,000) crore taka = 32,000 crore taka. At present, in the statistics of the international economy, the suffix Gross National Income (GNI) is used instead of Gross National Product (GNP).","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"The living standard of the people of that country is determined by that country's per capita income – Analyze.","marks":4,"answer":"According to the per capita income of the country described in the stem, it can be said that it is a low income country. Per capita income is the average income of the people of a country within a specific period of time. Per capita income is determined by two separate standards: 1. Gross National Income; and (2) Total population. Per capita national income or per capita income is found by dividing the Gross National Income (GNI) of any country in any specific period by the total population of that country. Per capita income can be expressed as below: Per Capita Income = Gross National Income / Total Population. The GNI of the country in the stem is 32,000 crore taka and the total population is 16 crore. Therefore, per capita income of the country = (32000 / 16) crore taka = 2000 Taka. That is, we can realize from the per capita income that the country is underdeveloped. Because according to the scale set by the World Bank, the per capita income of this country is less than the per capita income of developing countries. From this we can understand that the living standard of the people of this country is low and majority of the population does not have the ability to afford basic needs such as food, clothing, housing, education, medical treatment, etc. In conclusion, it can be said that National per capita income provides an idea of the standard of living of the majority population of the country. Hence, we can determine from the per capita income of the country in the stem that, the living standard of the people in that country are low.\n---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"The figure ‘M’ represents the characteristics of a developed country. A developed country is a country that has experienced economic development and this development has continued in the long run. The income growth rate of the people of these countries is high and their standard of living is high as well. These characteristics can be observed in the above country. The economy of developed countries is mainly dependent on industries. These countries have developed due to rapid industrialization. All these countries have become major industrial countries leaving behind the agriculture-based economy. From this discussion, it is evident that ‘M’ represents the characteristics of a developed country.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the importance of the factors in the economic development of Bangladesh on the basis of the stem.","marks":4,"answer":"The stimulus highlights the importance of GDP and GNP in the economic development of Bangladesh. GDP will include the value of final goods and services produced by all citizens, and foreign individuals, organizations and institutions living within the country. However, the income of local citizens and organizations or organizations living and working abroad will not be included in it. Their income will be included in GNP or Gross National Product. However, in calculating GNP, foreign income in the country should be excluded. The income of the stimulus Raju and his Chinese friend Su Chang working on Padma Bridge has been calculated in the gross domestic product or GDP sector. But his younger brother Rana's remittances from Canada will be counted in GNP. Because the income earned by the person living abroad will not be added to GDP. The impact of GDP on the economic development of Bangladesh is huge. GDP refers to the economic capacity of the country. GDP shows how big a country's economy is. On the other hand, GNP or national income determines the standard of living of a country. If its distribution is not balanced, then the standard of living of most people remains low even if per capita income increases. Therefore, proper distribution of GNP or national income is very important for the economic development of Bangladesh. Thus, it can be said that the importance of GDP and GNP in the development of the economy of Bangladesh is immense.\n---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What are the heavy and basic industries of Bangladesh?","marks":1,"answer":"The basic and heavy industries of Bangladesh are iron, steel, electricity, and energy industries.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Socio economic infrastructure is the foundation of economic development-Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"It is called the basis of economic development as the per capita real income of the people increases and equitable distribution of income is ensured through continuous development of socio-economic infrastructure. The increase in real per capita income over a long time along with the increase in gross national product or income of any country is called economic development. This is possible only when there are structural changes in the economy, such as the expansion of lending by banks and financial institutions, the use of advanced technology in production, the development of marketing practices, etc. As a result, people's income, savings, and investment power increases. Employment increases, unemployment decreases and living standards continue to improve. This condition is considered economic development. That is, natural improvement of socio-economic infrastructure is essential for economic development.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain in the light of case A how the national income of a country is measured by taking into account the produced goods and service?","marks":3,"answer":"A country's national income is measured by multiplying the total output of manufactured goods and services by their final market value. Gross national product or income is measured by the sum of the total monetary value of goods and services produced. To determine the national income in this method, the final price of goods and services has to be calculated. For example, if wood is produced from trees and chairs are produced from wood, the national product will be calculated only on the value of chairs. Because the price of the tree, wood, and labor is included in the price of the chair. Similarly, gross national product or income can be measured by multiplying the goods and services produced by a country's citizens by their final value. The gross national product and national income of a country are used synonymously. It can be measured in three ways. Namely - manufactured goods and services; income earned on the means of production; and the total cost to society. The results measured by all three methods are generally the same. So it can be said that the information of stem concept-1 indicates the said subject.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Case B indicated topic is an important determinant of any economy. Why? Give logic.","marks":4,"answer":"Per capita income determines the standard of living as mentioned in case B of stem. That is why, it is considered an important determinant in the economy of any country. Per capita income is the average income of the citizens of a country. National income or per capita income is obtained by dividing the total national income of a country by its population at a given time. This implies that Case B of stem refers to the per capita income concept of the economy. Per capita income determines the standard of living of a person. If the per capita income increases, the standard of living of the people improves, given that the price level of the goods of a country remains unchanged. However, one of its prerequisites is the balanced distribution of national income. Because of unequal distribution, the per capita income of most people will be lower than the national income. As a result, the quality of life of most people will not improve. For this reason, in countries with a balanced distribution of national income, the standard of living increases if per capita income increases and the price level remains unchanged. It is clear from the above discussion that, per capita income is an important determinant of any country's economy as it plays a role in determining the standard of living of the people.","image":null,"image_url":null}]
